newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian government rules out early poll.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian government rules out early poll.

text.p: The Bulgarian government on Saturday ruled out general elections demanded by opposition protesters who have besieged parliament for the past two days.

"The government of Bulgaria clearly states that violations of law and social order as well as immediate parliamentary elections at this moment are destructive for the country," a government statement said.
Security forces with clubs dispersed protesters early on Saturday, ending a 10-hour siege of parliament with what the statement described as "minimal use of force".
It said 178 civilians and 18 members of the security forces had been treated in hospital for injuries received in the clashes. One officer was in a critical condition.
"The opposition allowed the illegal mass rallies to mutate into crude violations of law and morality," the statement said.
"Order was restored in front of parliament and the deputies were led out of the building around 2 a.m. with minimal use of force."
Crisis talks between President Zhelyu Zhelev and political and security chiefs, including opposition leaders, ended without agreement on Saturday.

Yordan Sokolov, parliamentary leader of the opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF), warned they might no longer be able to control the protesters, who have staged six consecutive days of antigovernment rallies.
Zhelev, whose functions are largely ceremonial but who frequently criticises the governing Socialists, said he backed the opposition call for early elections.
"One can only hope to get out of the very serious situation with which we are confronted by organising early elections," Zhelev told the Paris newspaper Le Monde.
"Our country needs reforms which should be far more wide-ranging than those proposed by current political forces."
